fingerprint.structure: 7 slides: pov hook cover with a swipe arrow → 'the game has changed' (old advantage vs now) → 'what the numbers say' (one sourced stat block) → the main lesson (start with distribution) with a soft bio-link plug → contrarian lesson (don't be original) → next step (start building) naming one free tool → 'conclusion' recap, first-person founder credibility line, bio-link CTA
fingerprint.hook: 'pov: reality of building a <thing> <year>' in one bold line, mid-upper card, over a cutout of a deadpan man leaning back; mechanic: reality check / insider gap aimed at a builder identity, the swipe arrow promises the lessons
fingerprint.camera_motion: other:meme-cutout-text-card. Designed cards: flat warm light grey (#e4e3df), black and white cutout of a person (film-still look, waist up, cropped by the bottom edge) with a thick white sticker outline, some in a coarse halftone dot screen; text above it on the empty card
fingerprint.pacing: slideshow; cover 6 words; body slides 45 to 75 words in 3 to 5 short paragraphs of 1 to 3 lines (about 40 characters per line, hard line breaks)
fingerprint.text_overlay: heading: bold grotesk sans (Roboto or Inter Bold), black, lowercase, about 2.9% of frame height, left at x 13% (centred on the conclusion slide); body: monospace (Space Mono look), #111, lowercase except acronyms and brand names, about 1.95% of frame height, line pitch 2.3%, blank line between paragraphs, left aligned at x 13% (centred on the conclusion); no outline, no box
fingerprint.audio: 'original sound - stevelacyoffline' (a fan account's song upload), music only
fingerprint.arc: identity call-out (you're building a saas) → the old advantage is gone → the numbers are scary → but here's the order that works (distribution first) → reframe a fear (copied ideas are proof) → concrete next step → reassurance plus 'i do this myself' credibility → follow the link for more

layers.note: black and white film-still person, waist up, leaning back with one knee raised, deadpan stare at camera; coarse halftone dot screen; white sticker outline about 1.3% wide; bleeds off the bottom and left edges
thin black right arrow, swipe cue, bottom right

composition.balance: text upper third, person bottom left, arrow balances bottom right

frame.safe_zones: text at y 24 to 27% clears the top bar; the cutout sits under the caption zone, which is fine because it's art, not text
frame.quality: sharpness 583, noise 0.58, clutter 5.7 (halftone dots count as clutter)
frame.origin_realism: designed card; the person is a cut-out of a film still, not an original photo

text_blocks.text: pov: reality of building a saas 2026

other.what: a plain text card where a meme-energy cutout of a person sets the mood of each lesson
other.carrier: the text carries the message; the cutout is the emotional tag (smug, pointing, scheming, relaxed)
other.layout: text block upper half, cutout bottom left or bottom centre, cropped by the frame edge
other.type: bold sans heading + monospace body, lowercase, newsletter or terminal feel
other.palette: warm light grey card, pure black and white person, white outline
other.repeat: every slide repeats the card, the fonts and the cutout position; only the person and the text change
other.why: reads like a founder's private notes; the movie-still people add meme recognition and personality to a text-heavy post
other.risk: the source uses real actors from film stills; a replication must use original people

text_blocks.text:
most founders build for weeks,
launch, realize nobody's using it,
lose interest, and start a new idea.

do it the other way.

content first. …

don't overthink it. i see apps doing millions
of views with the simplest AI carousels you've
ever seen.

(link in bio to find creators already winning)
